correctness.rationale: A complete permutation DFA separates 0^a1^b and 1^b0^a exactly when some a-th and b-th powers in S_n fail to commute. For n≥5, each nontrivial power-generated subgroup is normal and contains nonabelian A_n; for n=1,2 no separation; the explicit S3,S4 subgroup tables give precisely the three coincident-defect corrections. The first nondivisor is always a prime power, with witnesses from lcm(1..q-1). Actual extracted checker passed 2,889 group cases, including all n=1..5 and a,b=1..24, and 19,999 arithmetic checks. Finite cases corroborate rather than prove the general group argument.

value.rationale: Exact minimum state counts for every two independent positive block lengths and an entire attainable-size spectrum classify a natural constrained word separation problem. The prime-power-only spectrum gives a structural impossibility for all composite non-prime-power sizes; the low-degree corrections exhibit nontrivial normal-subgroup centralization, not merely a numeric list. This does not purport to improve unrestricted worst-case separation bounds.
